title: Flushed out my cozy cleaning terraformer game prototype in HTML in about a week. Just re-built the whole game in Unity right when Astra dropped. Was surprised how easy it was.
author: 74BIT
selftext:
First of all this is my game design, my game vision, my art direction. Its not recreating someone else's idea. Not a one shot.

Yorick started off as a 2 week experiment with ChatGPT and Claude. You can see my old post where I blocked out the core gameplay, mechanics, aesthetics using AI. 

It was one of a bunch of small experiments I rapidly prototyped using AI. This one got the most traction overall. So I decided to flush out the game a bit more in HTML using Threejs. I was super happy being able to knock out a prototype of my own creation.

My goal is to put a game on Steam October Next fest, see if there is a big interest and add more content to the full game such as more unique planets, weird discoveries, interesting life forms, etc. 

Well, I finished the HTML prototype and had a few friends play it and they were hooked (the "cleaning dead matter" mechanic was a strong hook for them). As well as the engagement it got online. I was ahead of my own schedule. 

About that time Astra dropped. I tempted fate and asked "maybe I can rebuild the game in Unity before I submit for Next Fest?"

Well 3-4 days later (not full days as I have a full time job) The game was reproduced in Unity with a bit more polish, features and bugs fixed. 

Color me impressed. 

Also I built my own 3d models built in blockbench.

If you are interested the free demo is on Steam - "Yorick Worlds in Bloom"

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067090/Yorick\_Worlds\_in\_Bloom/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067090/Yorick_Worlds_in_Bloom/?beta=0)

comments.author: BoredzzzGame
comments.body: Looks cool! What was the workflow porting from 3rd to unity?

replies.author: 74BIT
replies.body: I worked on an HTML prototype for 2 weeks took a break then did a few more tweaks. Once I had the Prototype, I asked Astra to take my HTML, breakdown the game and create a plan how to port to Unity. I then directed it through each part of the plan and of course confirmed it did it correctly or met my standards. During this time I also created the core models (character, spirit animals, etc) in Blockbench. It then took those, made sure they were set up correctly for animation and put them in the game. To be clear, this was not one prompting. It took some direction and choices I needed to be made to make sure it was my core vision. Thats basically it. Going forward I will now start to prototype directly in Unity to save time. Hope that helps! Let me know if you have more questions
